register: wave-10 authoring register (S-B10 tranche) — part 1 of 2

items.stem: Write down the family formula that every carboxylic acid member follows.
items.modelAnswer: The general formula is CnH2n+1COOH, which can be shortened to RCOOH.

items.stem: How many alkyl carbons does the family formula count for methanoic acid, HCOOH?
items.modelAnswer: For methanoic acid the alkyl chain count n is zero — HCOOH carries just the carboxyl carbon.

items.stem: Explain why the n in CnH2n+1COOH does not count the carboxyl carbon itself.
items.modelAnswer: Because n counts only the alkyl chain; the COOH group is written separately at the end, so n never includes the carboxyl carbon.

items.stem: Propanoic acid has three carbons in total. Using the family formula CnH2n+1COOH, state the value of n for propanoic acid.
items.misconceptionClass: applying n to a named member
items.modelAnswer: n equals two for propanoic acid — two alkyl carbons plus the carboxyl carbon gives three in total.

items.stem: Name the first four carboxylic acids in order of chain length.
items.modelAnswer: Methanoic acid, ethanoic acid, propanoic acid and butanoic acid.

items.stem: What is vinegar, in terms of its composition?
items.modelAnswer: Vinegar is an aqueous solution of ethanoic acid, at about 5 percent by volume.

items.stem: Explain how the name ethanoic acid encodes the chain length of the acid.
items.misconceptionClass: naming law alkan plus oic acid
items.modelAnswer: The name is built as alkan plus oic acid, and the ethan root stands for the two-carbon alkyl chain.

items.stem: Give the molecular formula of the acid that follows ethanoic acid in the series, and name it.
items.modelAnswer: The next member is propanoic acid, CH3CH2COOH, with three carbons in total.

items.stem: State the catalyst used in the flask when preparing ethyl ethanoate.
items.modelAnswer: Concentrated sulfuric acid is the catalyst added to the ethanoic acid and ethanol.

items.stem: How is the ester separated from the reaction mixture as it forms?
items.modelAnswer: The ester is distilled off as soon as it forms and collected by condensation.

items.stem: Explain why distilling the ester away as it forms raises the amount of ester finally made.
items.modelAnswer: Removing the ester stops the reverse reaction from turning it back into the reactants, so more ester accumulates.

items.stem: A student proposes heating the flask with a Bunsen burner to speed the reaction up. State the hazard that rules this out and the safer equipment to use instead.
items.modelAnswer: Ethanol is flammable, so a naked Bunsen flame risks ignition; a water bath or electric heater is the safer choice.

items.stem: State the solution used to wash the acidic impurities out of the crude ester sample.
items.modelAnswer: Sodium carbonate solution removes the acidic impurities from the distillate.

items.stem: Which wash removes the leftover ethanol from the ester sample?
items.modelAnswer: Calcium chloride solution removes the leftover ethanol.

items.stem: Explain what the fizzing during the sodium carbonate wash tells you, and why it eventually stops.
items.modelAnswer: The fizzing is carbon dioxide escaping as the carbonate neutralises the acid impurities; it stops when no acid remains to react.

items.stem: After washing, a student waves a hand over the purified sample and notices a sweet, fruity smell. State what this observation confirms and name the class of compound present.
items.modelAnswer: The sweet smell confirms that an ester has formed — the sample contains ethyl ethanoate.

items.stem: Name the product trio from reacting a carboxylic acid with a metal carbonate.
items.modelAnswer: A salt, water and carbon dioxide are produced.

items.stem: Give the suffix that ends the name of every salt made from a carboxylic acid.
items.modelAnswer: Every such salt name ends in anoate.

items.stem: Ethanoic acid fizzes when magnesium is added. Name the gas and explain where it comes from.
items.modelAnswer: The gas is hydrogen — the metal displaces the acidic hydrogen from the COOH group of the acid.

items.stem: Methanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate in solution. State the name of the salt formed.
items.modelAnswer: The salt is sodium methanoate, formed alongside water and carbon dioxide.

items.stem: Give the balanced equation, in symbols, for ethanoic acid reacting with magnesium.
items.modelAnswer: 2CH3COOH + Mg gives (CH3COO)2Mg + H2.

items.stem: Name the three products when butanoic acid reacts with potassium carbonate.
items.modelAnswer: Potassium butanoate, water and carbon dioxide.

items.stem: Explain why two molecules of ethanoic acid are needed for every magnesium atom in the reaction equation.
items.misconceptionClass: two acids satisfy one metal ion
items.modelAnswer: Each ethanoate ion carries one negative charge, and magnesium forms 2+ ions, so two acid molecules are needed to satisfy the metal ion twice.

items.stem: Complete the symbol equation: 2CH3CH2CH2COOH + K2CO3 gives two molecules of the salt, plus water and carbon dioxide. State the formula of one salt molecule.
items.modelAnswer: Each salt molecule is CH3CH2CH2COOK — potassium butanoate.

items.stem: State the name given to the reaction between an alcohol and a carboxylic acid that makes an ester.
items.modelAnswer: The reaction is called esterification.

items.stem: State the small molecule released when the alcohol and the acid join to make the ester.
items.modelAnswer: A molecule of water is released as the reactants join.

items.stem: An ester formula is written CH3COOC2H5. Explain what the two parts on either side of the COO group represent.
items.misconceptionClass: two chains around the ester link
items.modelAnswer: The CH3CO part comes from the carboxylic acid chain and the C2H5 part comes from the alcohol chain, joined through the ester link.

items.stem: Propanol is reacted with ethanoic acid in the presence of the usual catalyst. Name the ester produced.
items.modelAnswer: The ester is propyl ethanoate.

items.stem: Name the ester formed when pentanol reacts with butanoic acid.
items.modelAnswer: The ester is pentyl butanoate.

items.stem: State the ending that the alcohol-derived part of an ester name always carries.
items.modelAnswer: The part from the alcohol always ends in yl.

items.stem: Explain why ethyl ethanoate, rather than the reactants it was made from, is chosen to carry a fruity scent in a food flavouring.
items.modelAnswer: Esters are volatile liquids with distinctive sweet smells, so the ester itself carries the fruity aroma while the acid and alcohol do not.

items.stem: An ester is named methyl butanoate. State which acid family member contributed its chain to this ester.
items.misconceptionClass: reading the acid from the oate part
items.modelAnswer: The acid partner is butanoic acid — the butanoate part of the name comes from the carboxylic acid.
